THE COMMITTEE ON PUBLIC SAFETY 4 Introduction Number 480-A, sponsored by Council Member Won. In 2020 the Council enacted The Public Oversight of Surveillance Technologies Act more commonly known as the POST Act. The POST Act aimed to improve transparency regarding the NYPD's acquisition and use of surveillance technologies by requiring the publishing of surveillance impact and use policies (IUPs) for each surveillance technology used by the Department. For each IUP, the NYPD documents the capabilities of the surveillance technology, the rules for access and use of such surveillance, and polices related to the retention, access, and use of data collection by such technologies. Further, the POST Act tasked the Department of Investigations, (DOI) with conducting annual audits of the NYPD’s IUPs. Proposed Introduction Number 168-A, sponsored by Majority Leader Farías, would strengthen the DOI’s capacity to conduct audits of the NYPD’s published IUPs by requiring the NYPD to provide DOI with semiannual updates on all newly acquired or discontinued surveillance technologies and updates to any data access and retention policies established in

Proposed Introduction Number 480-A, sponsored by Council Member Won, would clarify language in the POST Act to ensure increased transparency in IUPs published by the NYPD ensuring that IUPs are published for each distinct surveillance technology used by the Department; that such IUPs fully identify each entity that receives data gathered from such technology; that such IUPs report on specific safeguards in place to prevent unauthorized dissemination of surveillance data; and that such IUPs disclose evaluation of potential disparate impacts on protected groups arising from the NYPD’s use of such technologies. Additionally, NYPD would be required to develop policies regarding the circumstances under which data collected by the surveillance technology may be shared with external entities and develop an internal tracking system to monitor access of data granted to such entities.
